docs.syntax: =MID(text,FIND("-",text)+1,4) finds the separator then slices after it; criteria take patterns
docs.explain:
Two techniques meet on this table. The first places a slice relative to a separator. FIND reports where the hyphen sits, one is added to step past it, and MID reads four characters from there. Nothing in that formula is a typed position that depends on this table.

The second is a pattern in a criterion. AVERAGEIFS with "N*" picks the three North rows, and the amounts come to 380 across them, so the average rounds to 126.7. The pattern answers a question about rows, not about positions.

Each half fails differently. A missing hyphen breaks the slice with #VALUE!, while a pattern that matches no rows leaves AVERAGEIFS with nothing to divide and returns #DIV/0!. Checking which error you got tells you which half went wrong.

errors.text: FIND cannot see the hyphen in the code, so the MID call receives no start position.
No row matches the pattern, so AVERAGEIFS has no numbers to average.
Dropping the plus one returns -104, which is four characters starting at the hyphen.

docs.atWork: Slicing a code around its separator and averaging the rows that fit one pattern.
docs.outcome: Combine FIND with MID for a slice, and a wildcard criterion for a filtered average.
docs.teaches: MID driven by FIND beside a wildcard criterion, on one table
docs.dataset: Code, region and amount columns, sliced and matched

screens.prompt: In D2, read the four digits that follow the hyphen in the code in A2.

hints.syntax: =MID(A2,FIND("-",A2)+1,4): FIND locates the hyphen, MID reads from just after it.
hints.func-mid: The digits are a slice of the code, so MID reads them.
hints.func-find: The hyphen sits in a different place on each row, so FIND works it out.
hints.value: The hyphen is third, so the four digits start at four.
hints.error: Dropping the plus one returns -104, and the grader expects 1042.

reject.why: the start position is typed rather than found
the position is reported instead of the digits
starting one place late drops the first digit
the formula reads the second row rather than A2
there is no underscore to find
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In D2, round the average of the North amounts to one decimal place.

hints.syntax: ROUND wraps the average, so the pattern sits inside the AVERAGEIFS call and the digits come last.
hints.func-averageifs: A conditional average is AVERAGEIFS' job: the amounts first, the condition second.
hints.require-ref: The amounts to average are in C2:C5.
hints.value: 380 across three rows is 126.66, which rounds to 126.7.
hints.error: Averaging the region column puts text where numbers belong, so the cell shows #DIV/0!.

reject.why: the pattern never enters, so the South row is averaged in
the last North row is outside the range
the average is then divided by zero
the amount column is never read
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

seo.title: Slice text with FIND and MID in Excel
seo.description: FIND says where the separator sits and MID reads from there. A wildcard criterion on the same screen shows why a pattern answers a different question.
